explanation: The E138A mutation eliminates a negatively charged glutamate residue in the palm domain that, despite lacking direct ligand contact, likely participates in a network of electrostatic interactions that stabilize the NNRTI-binding pocket architecture. The loss of this charge coupled with the substantial decrease in side-chain volume (~50 Ų) creates a subtle conformational relaxation or repositioning of nearby pocket-forming residues, destabilizing the precise geometry required for optimal etravirine binding without causing a global structural collapse. This allosteric effect—mediated through the protein scaffold rather than direct drug contact—weakens etravirine affinity through accumulated loss of favorable electrostatic context and backbone/side-chain stabilization within the distant binding site.
